summary_paragraph: A woman with type 2 diabetes, gastroparesis, and recent right toe amputation was admitted for lower abdominal and flank pain, urinary frequency, and nausea, found to be in mild diabetic ketoacidosis. She had elevated blood glucose and an anion gap metabolic acidosis, managed with IV fluids and insulin, with resolution of DKA. Abdominal pain was not clearly linked to infection or obstruction—renal ultrasound was normal, and urinalysis showed no signs of UTI. Pain was managed with acetaminophen and tramadol, and her home diabetes and gastroparesis medications were resumed. Her hemoglobin dropped from 10.5 to 7.5, likely due to hemodilution, with no active bleeding. Chronic leukocytosis persisted but was deemed reactive. She remained stable, with no signs of infection in the foot wound, and was discharged home on her prior regimen with outpatient follow-up for CBC monitoring and diabetes management.
